q1_issues.issue: The attitude holder of the reporting verb is attached with Agent, but the propositional-attitude construction prescribes Experiencer for the holder of a speech/thought verb with a clausal complement.
The QuantifierPhrase companion is buried as a conjunct of the sealed rule's consequent instead of standing as its own top-level statement, so it becomes part of what each instance derives.
The proportion 'nearly one in 10' is never carried by a strength: the sealed Implication term has no STV slot, so the parse records an unquantified rule rather than a ~0.1 generalization.

'raise their risk of cancer by 25 percent or more' is encoded as (MeasureAtLeast (sk_raise $x) risk 25 percent), which states a risk-magnitude of the raising event rather than the size of the increase.

q2_gaps: numeric proportional quantifier over a bare kind ('nearly one in 10 people') — the quantifier-word-to-strength table covers all/most/many/few/no, and Fraction is scoped to 'of the' partitives, so there is no mapping for this
a quantified generic (an Implication whose quantity lives in its STV) sealed under a propositional attitude — a sealed term has no truth-value slot, so the quantity is unrepresentable
'raise / increase X by N percent' — a differential change of measure on an event has no licensed encoding (MoreBy is for comparatives between two entities)
notes: Sealing the reported content under Theme with no top-level flattening is right for a non-factive speech verb, and the US-researchers compound and its genus follow the compound rules.
